title: Allowance Uplift for Long Bench Time and Repeated Checks
content:
# Bench Standing Order: Uplift of the Allowance for Long Bench Time and Repeated Checks

## How the bench time is measured against the target

The target turnaround of a service level of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service is set in business days. Where the time a piece has been at the bench is compared with it, that target turnaround is counted in calendar days, taking 7 calendar days to 5 working days.

## The uplift

Where the time at the bench has run past the level's target turnaround taken at the long-delay multiple of 4, or the piece has been through more than one bench check, the allowance is taken half as much again — at a multiple of 1.5.

Where the time at the bench has run past that target turnaround but not past that multiple of it, and the piece has been through no more than one bench check, the allowance is taken a quarter as much again — at a multiple of 1.25.

In any other case the allowance is not uplifted on these grounds.

Whatever multiple the allowance is taken at, the figure it comes to is rounded to the nearest cent before it is added to the bench total.

## Reading the two grounds

The first ground is satisfied either by the time alone, running past the target turnaround taken at the long-delay multiple of 4, or by the checks alone, the piece having been through more than one bench check; either suffices. The second ground requires both of its parts: the time past the target turnaround but not past that multiple of it, and no more than one bench check. A bench check is any check logged against that work order, whatever the check found.

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

At a level whose target turnaround is 10 business days, that target counted in calendar days comes to 14 calendar days, and taken at the long-delay multiple of 4 it comes to 56 calendar days.

| Time at the bench | Bench checks logged | The allowance |
|---|---|---|
| 60 calendar days | 1 | taken half as much again, at 1.5 |
| 30 calendar days | 2 | taken half as much again, at 1.5 |
| 30 calendar days | 1 | taken a quarter as much again, at 1.25 |
| 10 calendar days | 1 | not uplifted on these grounds |
| 10 calendar days | 3 | taken half as much again, at 1.5 |

On the third row, an allowance of 212.37 USD taken a quarter as much again comes to 265.4625 USD, and the figure added to the bench total is that rounded to the nearest cent, 265.46 USD. An allowance of 84.71 USD taken a quarter as much again comes to 105.8875 USD, and the figure added is 105.89 USD.
